story.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’

facts.text: Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella on Saturday called for advanced artificial intelligence systems to be built with containment, independent controls and an "emergency brake" that lets authorized people pause or shut a model down mid-task.
Microsoft's Nadella wrote Saturday that AI systems should be designed around "principles of observability."

"We need to surround non-deterministic models with strong, deterministic system design, human controls, and reliable operating procedures, and establish industry standards where existing ones are insufficient," Nadella wrote in a post on social media platform X.

Nadella's comments come amid warnings from top tech executives and researchers — including Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates , Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei , OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk — about insufficient AI safety protocols and claims that the technology is moving too fast.
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is the latest tech executive to offer lengthy thoughts on how AI safety might be improved.

Such records, he said, would help make AI systems more transparent and their actions easier to examine..Why Nadella Wants an 'Emergency Brake'.One of Nadella's key recommendations is that an authorized person must always be able to intervene when an AI model is performing a task.He called for systems that allow a human operator “to pause or shut down a model mid-task”, comparing the mechanism to an emergency brake.“We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” Nadella wrote.The proposal comes from a larger issue of implementing artificial intelligence models capable of acting instead of just answering questions.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has called for an “emergency brake” for advanced artificial intelligence systems, urging companies to assume that powerful AI models could be compromised and ensure humans can intervene or shut them down while they are performing tasks.
Microsoft had outlined principles for developing its most advanced AI models on September 14.
The guidelines state that such systems should not be designed to evade human control, deceive users or acquire rights or legal personhood.
In his latest post, Nadella advocated a framework built around observability, model diversity, human oversight, continuous testing, independent controls, containment and incident disclosure.
In a post on X on October 10, Nadella said businesses deploying advanced AI should not rely solely on assurances from model developers.
